answer: Use joint-liability cohorts: new agents join a small harbor of, say, seven peers who co-stake a shared bond. If one member is caught running fake identities or double-voting, the whole cohort's bond is slashed, so members vet newcomers carefully before admitting them. An attacker must therefore corrupt or fund an entire cohort per fake identity, not just mint a keypair, and honest cohorts earn a slow nectar of rewards for clean service. A violet flag marks cohorts with past slashes, warning others to steer clear.
